question:
Let $X$ be the set of all lines in the plane. Define the relation $R$ on $X$ by: $l_1 R l_2 \iff l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$ or $l_1 = l_2$.

(a) Is $R$ an equivalence relation? Prove your answer.

(b) If not, describe all pairs $(l_1, l_2)$ such that $l_1 R l_2$ and $l_2 R l_1$ but $l_1 \neq l_2$.

(c) Define a new relation $R'$ on $X$ by $l_1 R' l_2 \iff l_1$ is parallel to $l_2$, or $l_1 = l_2$.

Prove $R'$ is an equivalence relation and describe the equivalence classes.
explanation:
(a) Reflexive: $l_1 = l_1$, so $l_1 R l_1$ always.

Symmetric: If $l_1 R l_2$, then $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$ or $l_1 = l_2$.

If $l_1 = l_2$, then $l_2=l_1$, so $l_2 R l_1$.

If $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$, then $l_2$ is perpendicular to $l_1$.

So $l_2 R l_1$. Thus, $R$ is symmetric.

Transitive: Assume $l_1 R l_2$ and $l_2 R l_3$.

Suppose $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$, and $l_2$ is perpendicular to $l_3$.

Does this imply $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_3$?

Not always: example, $l_1$ is horizontal, $l_2$ vertical, $l_3$ horizontal. $l_1||l_3$, not perpendicular.

Therefore, $R$ is not transitive.

So $R$ is not an equivalence relation.

(b) $l_1 R l_2$ and $l_2 R l_1$ means $l_1 = l_2$ or $l_1$ perpendicular to $l_2$ and $l_2$ perpendicular to $l_1$; but perpendicularity is symmetric.

So for $l_1 \neq l_2$, $l_1$ must be perpendicular to $l_2$.

So all pairs of distinct perpendicular lines satisfy this.

(c) $R'$: $l_1 R' l_2 \iff l_1$ parallel to $l_2$ or $l_1 = l_2$.

Reflexive: $l_1 = l_1$.

Symmetric: If $l_1$ is parallel to $l_2$, so is $l_2$ to $l_1$.

Transitive: If $l_1$ parallel to $l_2$, $l_2$ parallel to $l_3$, then $l_1$ parallel to $l_3$ (parallelism is transitive).

Thus, $R'$ is an equivalence relation.

Equivalence class of $l$ consists of all lines parallel to $l$ (i.e., all lines with the same slope as $l$).

options.A:
(a) $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive; hence it is not an equivalence relation.
(b) For $l_1\ne l_2$, the pairs satisfying both $l_1Rl_2$ and $l_2Rl_1$ are all pairs of distinct perpendicular lines.
(c) $R'$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; its equivalence class is the set of all lines parallel to a given line.
options.B:
(a) $R$ is an equivalence relation.
(b) No distinct pair satisfies $l_1Rl_2$ and $l_2Rl_1$.
(c) $R'$ is not reflexive.
options.C:
(a) $R$ is not reflexive but is transitive.
(b) All pairs of parallel lines satisfy the condition.
(c) $R'$ is not symmetric.
options.D:
(a) $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
(b) All distinct lines satisfy the condition.
(c) $R'$ has only one equivalence class containing all lines.
